title: Data & Statistics
subtitle: Mean, Median, Range, MAD
bounds: Data (PROTOCOL 4b): 3-7 whole-number values, each 0-20, sum <= 100. Every mean, median and MAD the correct working needs (old and new means/medians on outlier items included) is an integer 2-10 when it comes from a division (sum / count, halving two middles, distance-sum / count), so every division is a times-table fact. Ranges, odd-count medians and modes need no division. Missing value: total = mean x count (both <= 10), missing value 0-20. Outlier items: base of 4 values, the new value at least 10 from every base value; the mean moves strictly more than the median. Choices are integers (or the words Mean / Median) and never equal in value.

tiers.name: Range & Mode
tiers.description: Range is largest minus smallest. Mode is the value that shows up most often.

tiers.name: Median
tiers.description: Put the numbers in order; the median is the middle one (or halfway between the two middles).

tiers.name: Mean
tiers.description: Add the numbers, then divide by how many there are.

tiers.name: Missing Value & Outliers
tiers.description: Work back from a mean to a missing value; see which measure an outlier moves.

tiers.name: Mean Absolute Deviation
tiers.description: Average distance from the mean: find the mean, each distance, then their mean.

LARGEST.student: Range is largest minus smallest, not just the largest.
LARGEST.teacher: Gives the maximum value as the range.

FIRST_LAST.student: Find the largest and smallest first, wherever they sit in the list.
FIRST_LAST.teacher: Subtracts the first and last listed values instead of max minus min.

MOST_FOR_MODE.student: Mode is the value that shows up most often, not the biggest one.
MOST_FOR_MODE.teacher: Reads 'most' as 'largest' and gives the maximum as the mode.

COUNT_FOR_MODE.student: That's how many times it shows up. The mode is the value itself.
COUNT_FOR_MODE.teacher: Gives the frequency of the mode instead of the mode.

MISCOUNT.student: Count each value again. The mode shows up more times than any other.
MISCOUNT.teacher: Picks a repeated value that is not the most frequent one.

UNSORTED.student: Put the numbers in order first, then find the middle.
UNSORTED.teacher: Takes the middle of the list as written, without sorting.

MEAN_FOR_MEDIAN.student: That's the mean. The median is the middle number once they're in order.
MEAN_FOR_MEDIAN.teacher: Computes the mean when asked for the median.

ONE_MIDDLE.student: Two middle numbers? The median is halfway between them.
ONE_MIDDLE.teacher: With an even count, gives one of the two middle values.

NEXT_TO_MIDDLE.student: Cross off one number from each end until only the middle is left.
NEXT_TO_MIDDLE.teacher: Off by one on the middle position of the sorted list.

SUM_ONLY.student: Add them up, then divide by how many numbers there are.
SUM_ONLY.teacher: Stops at the sum; does not divide by the count.

MEDIAN_FOR_MEAN.student: That's the median. The mean is the sum divided by the count.
MEDIAN_FOR_MEAN.teacher: Gives the median when asked for the mean.

WRONG_COUNT.student: Count the numbers again, then divide the sum by that count.
WRONG_COUNT.teacher: Divides the sum by one more or one less than the number of values.

MEAN_AS_MISSING.student: The ? is not the mean. Find the total, then take away the others.
MEAN_AS_MISSING.teacher: Answers the given mean as the missing value.

TOTAL_ONLY.student: That's the total. Now take away the numbers you already know.
TOTAL_ONLY.teacher: Stops at mean x count; does not subtract the known values.

MISSING_NOT_COUNTED.student: The ? counts too: total = mean × how many numbers, ? included.
MISSING_NOT_COUNTED.teacher: Builds the total from mean x (count - 1), leaving out the missing value.

MEDIAN_MOVES.student: A far-off value pulls the mean a lot. The median barely moves.
MEDIAN_MOVES.teacher: Believes the median is more sensitive to an outlier than the mean.

RANGE_FOR_MAD.student: MAD is the average distance from the mean, not largest − smallest.
RANGE_FOR_MAD.teacher: Gives the range as the MAD.

MEAN_FOR_MAD.student: That's the mean. Now average each number's distance from it.
MEAN_FOR_MAD.teacher: Stops at the mean; never finds the deviations.

SUM_DEVIATIONS.student: You added the distances. Now divide by how many numbers there are.
SUM_DEVIATIONS.teacher: Sums the absolute deviations without dividing by the count.
